steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Remember to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment (<></>) for now.
steps.hint: Define the component after your imports. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create your App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component. This will serve as the root component for your Progressive Web App.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a component named App that returns an empty fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Create a functional component named App that returns an empty fragment (<></>).

steps.title: Initialize state for install prompt
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'deferredPrompt' and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: Call useState(null) and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'deferredPrompt' ready to store the PWA installation prompt.
successCriteria: The App component contains a useState call that creates 'deferredPrompt' initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the state variable that will hold the PWA installation prompt.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a variable named 'deferredPrompt' with an initial value of null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization isn't quite right. Use useState(null) to create a variable named 'deferredPrompt'.

steps.title: Initialize state for installation status
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create a state variable named 'isInstalled' and initialize it to false.
steps.hint: Add a new useState call after the existing deferredPrompt state. The syntax is similar to what you already have for deferredPrompt.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a boolean state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: deferredPrompt and isInstalled, with isInstalled initialized to false.
successCriteria: The isInstalled state variable is declared using useState and initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added state to track whether the PWA is installed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable named 'isInstalled' with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to add a new useState call for 'isInstalled' with an initial value of false.

steps.title: Define beforeinstallprompt handler
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleBeforeInstallPrompt that takes an event parameter and saves the event to the deferredPrompt state using setDeferredPrompt.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives the event and updates the state. The event object contains the prompt that can be triggered later.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleBeforeInstallPrompt function that updates the deferredPrompt state with the event object.
successCriteria: The handleBeforeInstallPrompt function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setDeferredPrompt(event) inside its body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the event handler that captures the PWA installation prompt. This will allow you to save the prompt for later use.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the handler, but make sure it takes an event parameter and calls setDeferredPrompt(event) to save the prompt.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handler isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function named handleBeforeInstallPrompt that updates the deferredPrompt state with the event.

steps.title: Define install handler function
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleInstall that will trigger the saved installation prompt and update the installation status.
steps.hint: Define a function inside your App component that will use the deferredPrompt state to show the installation prompt and update isInstalled state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleInstall is defined inside the App component, ready to implement PWA installation logic.
successCriteria: The handleInstall function is defined inside the App component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the handleInstall function. This will be used to trigger the PWA installation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a function named handleInstall inside the App component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInstall function is not defined correctly. Please create a function named handleInstall inside your App component.

steps.title: Define appinstalled handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleAppInstalled that updates the isInstalled state to true when the PWA is successfully installed.
steps.hint: Define a function inside your component that calls setIsInstalled with the value true.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function handleAppInstalled is defined that updates the installation status state.
successCriteria: The handleAppInstalled function is defined and calls setIsInstalled(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a handler that will detect when the PWA is successfully installed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function calls setIsInstalled with the value true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleAppInstalled that updates the isInstalled state.

steps.title: Add useEffect for event listeners
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook inside your App component to attach the 'beforeinstallprompt' and 'appinstalled' event listeners when the component mounts.
steps.hint: Import useEffect from React, then call useEffect with an empty dependency array to run code once on mount. Inside the effect, add event listeners to the window object that call your handler functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook is added with an empty dependency array, containing event listeners for 'beforeinstallprompt' and 'appinstalled' events.
successCriteria: useEffect is imported and called with an empty dependency array, and event listeners are attached to window for both 'beforeinstallprompt' and 'appinstalled' events.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the useEffect hook to set up PWA event listeners when the component mounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both event listeners and imported useEffect from React.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Remember to import useEffect, then add it with an empty dependency array and attach both event listeners to the window object.

steps.title: Return main container structure
steps.instruction: In your App component, replace the current return statement with a main container div that has the class name 'app-container'.
steps.hint: The return statement should render a div element with the appropriate class attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a div with the class 'app-container' as the main layout container.
successCriteria: The return statement renders a div element with className='app-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main container structure for your PWA. This will serve as the foundation for adding UI elements.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element with the exact class name 'app-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should render a div element with className='app-container'. Check your JSX syntax.

steps.title: Add header with app title
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a header element containing an h1 with the text 'PWA Demo'.
steps.hint: The header should be a semantic HTML element that wraps the heading. Use JSX syntax to add the elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will display a header with the title 'PWA Demo' when rendered.
successCriteria: The component returns a header element containing an h1 with the exact text 'PWA Demo'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the app title header, which establishes the app's identity.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some structure, but make sure you have a header element with an h1 containing 'PWA Demo'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header with the app title is missing. Check that you've added a header element with an h1 containing 'PWA Demo' in the return statement.

steps.title: Add installation status display
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph inside your component's return statement that displays the current installation status based on the isInstalled state.
steps.hint: Use the isInstalled state variable to conditionally display different text messages about installation status.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph that indicates whether the PWA is currently installed or not, using the isInstalled state value.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added that displays installation status based on the isInstalled state variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the current installation status. This helps users understand whether the PWA is already installed on their device.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but it might not be correctly using the isInstalled state. Make sure the paragraph displays different text based on whether isInstalled is true or false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph displaying installation status is missing or incorrect. Add a paragraph element that shows whether the app is installed using the isInstalled state variable.

steps.title: Add install button and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside your component's return statement that triggers the install handler when clicked and is disabled when the app is already installed.
steps.hint: Place the button after the header. Use the onClick prop to call your install handler function and the disabled prop to conditionally disable it based on the isInstalled state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler and conditional disabling
<button onClick={handleClick} disabled={isDisabled}>
  Click me
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears in the UI that users can click to install the PWA, which becomes disabled once installation is complete.
successCriteria: A button element is added with onClick calling the install handler and disabled conditionally based on isInstalled state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the install button with proper click handling and conditional disabling.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has both onClick and disabled props correctly implemented.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the required onClick handler and disabled condition.
